chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī Maryam, who said:

I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who performs wudu (ablution), then calls his bondwoman and she takes him by the hand until he reaches the mosque? For indeed, some people among us claim that this is the touching referred to as al-mulāmasah.
So he said: No, by Allah, there is no harm in that, and I have perhaps done that myself, and what is meant by this is not that.
It only means sexual intercourse in the private part.

key_terms.الْمُلَامَسَةُ: touching, as discussed in legal interpretation
key_terms.مَا بِذَلِكَ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm or problem in that

ai.seo_question: Does touching a woman by the hand break wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that merely touching a woman by the hand does not invalidate wudu (ablution). Imam Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام interprets the Qur'anic phrase “أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ” as referring specifically to sexual intercourse. The report is significant in Shia fiqh for clarifying ritual purity rulings through Qur'anic interpretation transmitted from the Imam عليه السلام.
